kar-c6c1809d.name: Vadiraja Tirtha
kar-c6c1809d.role: 20th pontiff of Sode Maṭha (Udupi Aṣṭa Maṭha) in the Madhva succession
kar-c6c1809d.contrib: Reformed the Paryaya from two months to two years (c.1532); renovated the Udupi Krishna temple; consecrated Dharmasthala Manjunatha; built the Trivikrama temple at Sode; entered brindavana alive (sajiva).

kar-813911b2.name: Jayatirtha (Tikacharya)
kar-813911b2.place: on the Kagina river, Kalaburagi district
kar-813911b2.contrib: Systematised and defended Dvaita to full dialectical parity. Nyaya Sudha became the central curricular text of every Madhva matha ('Sudha' study is the summit of the tradition).
works: Nyaya Sudha (magnum opus, ~24,000 granthas, on Anuvyakhyana)
Prameya Dipika / Nyaya Dipika (on Gita Bhashya)

kar-4d34b6e8.name: Raghavendra Tirtha (Rayaru)
kar-4d34b6e8.contrib: The best known figure of the whole line, honoured as Parimalacharya for his commentary Parimala on Jayatirtha's Nyaya Sudha. Born Venkatanatha at Bhuvanagiri and trained by Sudhindra Tirtha, he left an oeuvre spanning commentaries on Madhva, Jayatirtha and Vyasatirtha, nine Khandarthas on the Upanishads, and a treatise on Purva Mimamsa, besides devaranamas composed under the signature Venu Gopala. He entered his vrindavana alive at Manchale (Mantralaya) in 1671, where his shrine draws vast numbers of pilgrims to this day.

kar-78e6cce5.name: Vijayindra (Vijayeendra) Tirtha
kar-78e6cce5.contrib: A polymath and relentless polemicist trained under Vyasatirtha and Surendra Tirtha, credited by tradition with 104 works across Vedanta, Purva Mimamsa, Nyaya and poetics and with mastery of the sixty-four arts. Holding the seat at Kumbakonam under the Thanjavur Nayakas, he is renowned for his debates with the Advaita scholar Appayya Dikshita; inscriptions record village grants won through his victories.

kar-951bbf8d.name: Sumatindra Tirtha

A prolific author of more than forty works — commentaries, tippanis on the Sudha and Chandrika, and independent treatises — his vrindavana is at Srirangam.

kar-77473a83.name: Vishveshwara Tirtha (Pejawara)
kar-77473a83.role: 16th pontiff of Pejawara Maṭha (Udupi Aṣṭa Maṭha) in the Madhva succession
kar-77473a83.contrib: 16th pontiff in the Pejawara Maṭha succession (Udupi Aṣṭa Maṭha), the paryāya lineage descending from Madhvācārya’s disciple Adhokshaja Tirtha.

kar-495cad53.name: Srinidhi Tirtha
kar-495cad53.contrib: Disciple of Srikantha Tirtha and guru of Vidyanidhi Tirtha; his vrindavana is at Pallipalayam.

kar-fc58d678.name: Srinivasa Tirtha
kar-fc58d678.contrib: Pontifical successor of Vyasatirtha in the Sosale line.

kar-25532dc6.name: Vijayindra (Vijayeendra) Tirtha
kar-25532dc6.contrib: A polymath and relentless polemicist trained under Vyasatirtha and Surendra Tirtha, credited by tradition with 104 works across Vedanta, Purva Mimamsa, Nyaya and poetics and with mastery of the sixty-four arts. Holding the seat at Kumbakonam under the Thanjavur Nayakas, he is renowned for his debates with the Advaita scholar Appayya Dikshita; inscriptions record village grants won through his victories.

kar-c016446d.name: Vijayindra (Vijayeendra) Tirtha
kar-c016446d.contrib: A polymath and relentless polemicist trained under Vyasatirtha and Surendra Tirtha, credited by tradition with 104 works across Vedanta, Purva Mimamsa, Nyaya and poetics and with mastery of the sixty-four arts. Holding the seat at Kumbakonam under the Thanjavur Nayakas, he is renowned for his debates with the Advaita scholar Appayya Dikshita; inscriptions record village grants won through his victories.

kar-d5fcd67e.name: Sripadaraja (Lakshminarayana Tirtha)
kar-d5fcd67e.contrib: Pioneer of the Haridasa movement and dasa-sahitya; credited with inventing the 'suladi' form; teacher of Vyasaraja; advisor to Saluva Narasimha.

kar-3a9f382e.name: Satyaparakrama Tirtha
kar-3a9f382e.place: Chittapur, Kalaburagi district, Karnataka (bank of Krishna)
kar-3a9f382e.contrib: Disciple of Satyeshti Tirtha, author of the Prameyamala and a stotra on Satyavrata Tirtha. He held the seat 1872-1879; his vrindavana is at Chittapur in the Kalaburagi region on the bank of the Krishna.

kar-4e0aeff1.name: Satyasandha Tirtha
kar-4e0aeff1.place: Mahishi, Tirthahalli taluk, Shivamogga district, Karnataka
kar-4e0aeff1.contrib: Stressed unity among Madhva mathas; discouraged sectarian division.

kar-44915d02.name: Satyabhinava Tirtha
kar-44915d02.place: Nachiarkoil, near Kumbhakonam, Thanjavur district, Tamil Nadu
kar-44915d02.contrib: Codified 17 categories of daily temple worship with 64 sevaks.

kar-f87c2a7e.name: Sumatindra Tirtha
kar-f87c2a7e.contrib: The third pontiff after Raghavendra Tirtha, whom his guru had singled out with the words that the third yati after him would carry his works forward; he is accordingly called the Vidyasuta (intellectual heir) of Raghavendra. A prolific author of more than forty works — commentaries, tippanis on the Sudha and Chandrika, and independent treatises — his vrindavana is at Srirangam.

kar-09d67067.name: Satyadharma Tirtha
kar-09d67067.contrib: A pontiff of the Navaratna family (1797-1830) who wrote a commentary on the Bhagavata. His vrindavana at Holehonnur is built so that the amshas of Jayatirtha, Vadiraja, Raghavendra and Satyabodha are held to be present there, with a Shiva-Bhagirathi sannidhana beside the garbhagudi.

kar-05f33686.name: Satyapramoda Tirtha
kar-05f33686.contrib: Leading modern defender of Dvaita; founded the Jayateertha Vidyapeetha, Bangalore (1989); relocated older brindavanas during dam-building.

kar-d91d93e0.name: Satyapramoda Tirtha
kar-d91d93e0.contrib: Leading modern defender of Dvaita; founded the Jayateertha Vidyapeetha, Bangalore (1989); relocated older brindavanas during dam-building.

kar-ba056240.name: Satyaprajna Tirtha
kar-ba056240.place: Atkur, near Raichur, Karnataka (bank of Krishna)
kar-ba056240.contrib: Served as Divan (administrator) of the matha before ordination.

kar-fe5f1f87.place: Nachiarkoil, near Kumbhakonam, Thanjavur district, Tamil Nadu
kar-fe5f1f87.contrib: Codified 17 categories of daily temple worship with 64 sevaks.

kar-267e59c7.place: Nachiarkoil, near Kumbhakonam, Thanjavur district, Tamil Nadu
kar-267e59c7.contrib: Codified 17 categories of daily temple worship with 64 sevaks.

kar-a05cfe50.name: Surottama Tirtha (Bhandarakeri (Barkur))
kar-a05cfe50.contrib: 14th pontiff in the Bhandarakeri (Barkur) succession, the lineage recorded from Satya Tirtha in the community genealogical table.

kar-4d01d792.name: Dheerendra Tirtha
kar-4d01d792.contrib: Purvashrama son of Vadindra Tirtha, long reluctant to take sannyasa and much given to touring and preaching. He eventually received sannyasa directly before Vijayindra Tirtha's shrine at Kumbakonam, held the Mantralaya seat only briefly, and then settled at Hosaritti on the Varada river. He was close to Satyabodha Tirtha and Jagannatha Dasa, who is said to have composed the Harikathamrutasara in his presence. He wrote several commentaries on Upanishadic hymns.
